name: wame
description: Claude Code plugins by WAME — developer productivity tools for teams

plugins.name: git-commit
plugins.description: Turn the current working tree into one or more logical git commits using the TYPE(scope): Message convention from the user's global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Title and body always in English; TYPE and scope inferred from the changes. When the run is tied to a task, the task ID is appended in square brackets — TYPE(scope)[<task-id>]: Message — detected from $ARGUMENTS, --task=<id>, or current branch name (feature/teamwork-task-<id>, task/<id>, ...). When no task ID is detected, the brackets are omitted entirely (never empty []). Groups related changes into one commit each; pass --all-in-one to skip grouping. Never adds Co-Authored-By lines, never pushes, never amends. Singular 'git-commit' — distinct from the 'git-commits-history' plugin which summarises historical commits.

plugins.name: git-commits-history
plugins.description: Fetch and summarize git commits history across all repositories for a date range. Shows timeline with AI-powered summaries, file changes, and project breakdown. Supports GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket. Renamed from 'git-commits' in v2.0.0 — existing users see /Migration in README; config in ~/.claude/plugins/data/git-commits-wamesk/ is preserved automatically.

plugins.name: git-commits
plugins.description: [DEPRECATED] Renamed to 'git-commits-history'. Installing or updating this plugin shows migration instructions only. Run: /plugin uninstall git-commits@wamesk && /plugin install git-commits-history@wamesk. Config in ~/.claude/plugins/data/git-commits-wamesk/ is preserved across the rename.

plugins.name: laravel-docs
plugins.description: Generate Laravel project specifications (technical, business, admin navigation) for individual models or modules. Auto-detects modular (wamesk/*, Modules/*) vs flat (app/Models) project structure. Configurable output paths, per-project config, and replaceable prompts per documentation type.

plugins.name: dnr-business
plugins.description: Generate a WAME 'Detailný návrh riešenia' (DNR) — the binding pre-development project document — as a branded .docx. Accepts a folder, file(s), or free-form description as input; if invoked inside an existing project repository, deep-analyses modules/architecture for richer context. Outputs a client-language (sk/cs/en) Word document in WAME visual identity (green #20E87A, navy #091145, Inter font), with mandatory sections (Východiskový stav, Ciele, Popis riešenia, Technické riešenie, Fázy, Riziká, Podmienky). Sections 'Fázy' and 'Riziká' (min. 5) are schema-enforced. Never invents client data — uses [DOPLNIŤ] placeholders and reports them as open follow-ups. Since 1.3.0 phase 'trvanie' follows the WAME estimate methodology `wame-estimate-v2` — one number per task picked against fixed outcome anchors, no speedup factor and no risk buffer — per-task minutes rolled up to whole weeks as the lower bound, plus the estimated cost of everything still undecided in that phase (open questions, [DOPLNIŤ] items, client-side dependencies) as the upper bound, always published as a range (e.g. '3–4 weeks'). The flat +25–35 % reserve that used to widen the range is gone — it padded the same risk a second time.

plugins.name: teamwork-tasks-from-dnr
plugins.description: Generate Teamwork.com import-ready task plan (XLSX + Markdown) from a 'Detailný návrh riešenia' (DNR) document. LLM-powered extraction of tasklists, business-friendly task names, acceptance criteria, and technical plans. Multi-language (sk/en/cs). Works as Claude Code plugin and Claude.ai Skill with the same SKILL.md. Since 1.6.0 tasks that add a screen carry cross-cutting acceptance criteria under `### Prierezové požiadavky` — reachability (a menu entry and links from the parent screen, enforced by the validator) plus the applicable security, performance and UI/UX items, keyed like teamwork-task-test's QA dimensions — and every code task's technical plan ends with a Framework line naming the framework versions detected from the repository's lock files (a generic line when none are detected), plan only and never an acceptance criterion; the frontend contract lookup no longer aborts in zsh and the orchestrator script is found in the plugin cache (highest installed version). Since 1.5.0 the generated task descriptions never carry the estimate — it goes to the ESTIMATED TIME column alone. Since 1.4.0 the per-task estimates follow the WAME estimate methodology `wame-estimate-v2` — one number per task picked against fixed outcome anchors, no speedup factor and no risk buffer, with the anchors documented in SKILL.md; the DNR's man-days stay the hard total and the methodology governs how that budget is split, with any compromise reported in `warnings`. Since 1.3.0 a contract-first flow detects the repository (backend/frontend/standalone via composer.json / @ionic packages); in a Laravel backend repo it generates a deterministic, redocly-clean OpenAPI 3.1 contract skeleton + data-model from the DNR under docs/contracts/<feature>/ (shared WameSuccess/WameError envelope, Sanctum bearer, x-wame-status: draft, valid even with [DOPLNIŤ]), writes idempotently (existing files become *.proposed + diff, never silently overwritten), adds a 'Definovať API kontrakt' predecessor task with its own MD estimate, and appends a ### Kontrakt block to every API task so backend and frontend can run in parallel; frontend repos only reference an existing contract, standalone runs list it under ## Chýbajúce artefakty. Opt out with --no-contract; never runs git.

plugins.name: teamwork-task
plugins.description: Fetch Teamwork.com tasklist/task by URL (including task comments — by default the newest comment is always read and the full thread whenever the description is thin or refers to it), render a plan for approval, then implement each task in the current repository, commit per task using TYPE(scope)[<task-id>]: Message convention, and log spent time back to Teamwork via the REST API v3 as sequential, non-overlapping entries (both start time and duration aligned to the 5-minute rounding step). Time-log descriptions are written in a business tone (what was delivered for the user/business), technical detail only when needed for identification. Reads the acceptance criteria from the `## Akceptačné kritériá` / `## Acceptance criteria` block of the canonical WAME description (first-HR split as the fallback) and takes the final summary as the goal. Configurable plan mode (overview | per_task | none), time tracking (real time rounded to 5 minutes, or ask) and branching strategy (current branch or new feature branch). When the companion `teamwork-task-test` skill is installed, hands off to it automatically at the end, together with the build-time quality notes, so each task's acceptance criteria get individually verified before push (default ON, disable with --test-after=false). Persistent config (API token survives plugin updates). Pauses and asks via AskUserQuestion on blockers. Push is left to the user. Since 1.5.0 comments, subtasks, attachments, the tasklist column filter and board moves really work: four independent defects (a comment sort key v3 rejects with HTTP 400, a `commentsCount` gate on a field v3 never returns, a non-existent timestamp field, and `echo "$JSON" | jq` pipes that break in zsh) each let a run continue with no comments and no error; the project id now comes from `.tasklist.meta.projectId`, an explicit `false` in the config is respected, and every failed request or parse prints a ⚠ line. It follows the new WAME board: a tasklist run implements only tasks in a start column (`tasklist_filter.todo_stages`, default Ready for Development and To Do) assigned to you — a task not on the board is analyse-only — and a finished task moves to Done - Local (fallbacks Internal testing → Testing for older boards); existing configs are migrated once, only where they still hold the old defaults. A completed task behind a single-task URL is processed only after you confirm. Every task is also planned, built and self-checked against five build-time quality dimensions shared with teamwork-task-test — UI/UX & accessibility, performance, security, page reachability (a new screen ships with its menu entry and inbound links in the same commit) and framework best practices (new or changed code uses the idioms of the versions detected from the project's lock files, checked in current docs, without drive-by rewrites) — configurable with build_quality.dimensions or --dimensions.

plugins.name: teamwork-task-test
plugins.description: Fetch a Teamwork.com task or whole tasklist by URL, extract acceptance criteria, and verify each criterion against the current repository — by running existing Pest / PHPUnit / Dusk / Cypress / Playwright / Vitest / Jest / Selenium tests where possible, by driving a real browser via the chrome-devtools MCP for visual checks, and by writing concrete manual scenarios for everything that cannot be automated. Beyond the stated criteria it always reviews four cross-cutting dimensions over the task's own diff — UI/UX and accessibility, performance, security, and page reachability (every registered screen must be reachable by clicking, not only by typing its URL) — plus an advisory fifth, framework best practices, and proves every passing test is load-bearing with a negative control. Outputs a per-task report where each acceptance criterion is marked ✅ verified / ⚠️ partial / ❌ failed / 📋 manual / 📝 proposed, plus a separate findings table for the review dimensions and a short section of framework recommendations. Ticks met criteria to [x] in the Teamwork description under a byte-exact safety contract that preserves inline images; never moves the task or posts comments unless the user opts in. Shares the API token config with the `teamwork-task` plugin so setup is one-time. Since 1.2.0 task comments are really read: a `commentsCount` gate on a field Teamwork v3 never returns and a sort key the API rejects with HTTP 400 each let QA run on no comments without an error — comments are now always fetched with a valid sort, an HTTP check and a v1 fallback, and a failure is reported as 'comments unavailable', never as 'no comments'. Acceptance criteria are read from the `## Akceptačné kritériá` block of the canonical WAME format instead of the reporter's preamble above it, the project id from `.tasklist.meta.projectId`, and every snippet is zsh-safe. The new `framework` dimension only recommends the idioms of the framework versions the project actually has installed (detected from lock files, checked in current docs, at most five per task): it never edits code, never fails, downgrades or blocks a criterion, and is marked `advisory: true` in ac.json — only a feature newer than the installed version or the browserslist target, which will not run, stays a real finding.

plugins.name: teamwork-task-analyze
plugins.description: Fetch a Teamwork.com task or whole tasklist by URL and prepare it for implementation. Pulls the task name, description, attachments, comments, comment-attached files, and subtasks via REST API v3 (reusing the shared config/token from the teamwork-task plugin), deep-scans the current repository for related code/specs, then interactively rewrites the task description into the canonical WAME format — additively, keeping everything the reporter already wrote verbatim at the top (inline screenshots and links included) and never writing the estimate into the description or the title: [optional preamble] → HR → Akceptačné kritériá → HR → Cieľ → HR → Technický popis (Claude Code Plan-Mode output — files, functions, DB schema, step-by-step, edge cases). Pauses with AskUserQuestion (in batches of 4, up to 6 per run) for every clarifying question that arises and folds the answers back into the new description; anything unresolved is preserved as [OTVORENÉ] markers. Reviews existing subtasks (updates outdated ones, proposes splitting tasks above 240 min into 2–6 atomic subtasks when AC have natural cut points; never forces a split for small tasks). Checks the time estimate using the WAME estimate methodology `wame-estimate-v2` — one number per task against fixed outcome anchors, no speedup factor and no risk buffer — sets one when missing, otherwise shows a highlighted warning with original vs proposed estimate + reasoning and asks before overwriting. Every Teamwork write is preceded by a preview and an explicit AskUserQuestion confirmation; --write-back=never gives a full dry-run. For tasklist URLs reuses the teamwork-task filter — only tasks in a configured start column (default 'Ready for Development' or 'To Do') assigned to the current user are analysed for write-back; tasks not on the board and everything else are listed read-only so the user can sanity-check teammates' work. Read-only against the board (never moves it) and against time logs (never writes one). Since 1.3.0 comments, attachments, subtasks, the board column and the project link come from fields and endpoints Teamwork v3 actually has — an invalid comment sort key, a `commentsCount` gate, a `cardId` column lookup and a missing `projectId` had silently produced no comments, no eligible tasks and a /projects/null link — a failed fetch is named as unavailable, and an explicit `false` in the config sticks. The start columns follow the new WAME board (`tasklist_filter.todo_stages`, migrated with exactly teamwork-task's rule). Rewritten acceptance criteria gain a `### Prierezové požiadavky` block with the cross-cutting requirements that apply (menu entry and inbound links for a new screen, object-scoped authorization, data volume, UI states) under the ui_ux / performance / security / reachability keys teamwork-task-test verifies, and the technical plan names the installed framework versions and the idiom to use — plan only, never an acceptance criterion.

plugins.name: teamwork-tasks-from-desk
plugins.description: Turn a Teamwork.com Desk ticket into a structured Teamwork.com Projects task (plus optional subtasks) without leaving the terminal. User provides a Desk ticket URL; plugin fetches the ticket — subject, customer, chronological message thread (replies + internal notes) and email attachments — via the Teamwork Desk REST API, asks for a Teamwork Projects URL (project or tasklist) so it knows where to file the work, and for an assignee email (may be empty for unassigned). When the proposed task naturally splits into multiple roles (BE/FE/QA/migration), the plugin asks for an email per role. Using the WAME canonical task format ([preamble] → HR → ## Akceptačné kritériá → HR → ## Cieľ → HR → ## Technický popis) the plugin synthesises a draft main task — title, description, optional subtasks, per-task estimate, written to the Teamwork estimate field and never into the task title or description (WAME estimate methodology `wame-estimate-v2` — one number against fixed anchors, 15-minute step, split-proposal above 240 min, 480-minute cap) — and asks clarifying questions via AskUserQuestion in batches of 4 (max 6 per run). The ticket's email attachments are mapped to the right task or subtask via AskUserQuestion. After a full preview + confirmation the plugin creates the main task and each confirmed subtask via /projects/api/v3, uploads attachments via the pending-file flow and attaches them. The main task is linked back to the Desk ticket (native Desk-link attribute when available, otherwise the ticket URL in the description footer). At the end the plugin posts an internal note in the Desk thread (link to the new Projects task + a structured summary of what was prepared) and offers to draft a customer-facing reply — the draft is ALWAYS posted as an internal note for review, NEVER sent to the customer; the plugin never touches the Desk replies endpoint. Reuses the Teamwork plugin family's shared API token config; the separate Desk API key is stored alongside under teamwork.desk_token. Never replies to the Desk customer, never moves the Desk ticket on its board, never logs time, never moves tasks on the Projects board, never runs git. Since 1.3.0 every snippet runs correctly under zsh (Claude Code's shell on macOS) — attachments and subtask attachments, the Desk call helper, the customer and inbox names and threads longer than 100 messages had been silently lost — attachments keep their real file names, every read checks its HTTP status, and the retry guard recognises the task it just created instead of creating a duplicate. The drafted task also carries a `### Prierezové požiadavky` block with the cross-cutting requirements that apply (reachability via a menu entry and links from related screens, security, performance, UI/UX), keyed like teamwork-task-test's QA dimensions, and a technical-plan line naming the installed framework versions and their current idioms (plan only, never an acceptance criterion); none of it reaches the customer-facing draft.

plugins.name: teamwork-tasks-from-session
plugins.description: Turn the work you just did in a Claude Code session into a Teamwork.com Projects task (plus optional subtasks) — for the common case where you start solving a problem in Claude Code before a task even exists. Reconstructs what the session accomplished (git commits + working-tree diff made since the session started, changed files, repo shape, and the live conversation context), drafts a main task in the canonical WAME format ([preamble] → HR → ## Akceptačné kritériá → HR → ## Cieľ → HR → ## Technický popis), proposes 2–6 atomic subtasks when the estimate exceeds 240 min and the work has natural cut points, and computes a `wame-estimate-v2` estimate, written to the Teamwork estimate field and never into the task title or description, shown next to the real logged session time — this plugin is the methodology's only measured feedback loop. It logs the REAL session duration back to Teamwork: the session start comes from a bundled SessionStart hook, falling back to the end of today's last timelog, the newest session transcript and finally asking — always shown as an editable proposal and clamped so it never overlaps an existing timelog (one sequential, 5-minute-aligned, business-tone entry). If no Teamwork URL is passed the skill asks where to file the work; a project or tasklist URL creates a new main task there, a single-task URL files the session work as a subtask of that task. Asks via AskUserQuestion which Teamwork email to assign the task to (you by default, unassigned, or a colleague). Everything is shown in a full preview + confirmation gate before any write (--write-back=never is a full dry-run), and after creating the task the skill asks per run what to do with the board — leave it, move it to the done column (the shared board_workflow target teamwork-task uses: Done - Local, fallbacks Internal testing → Testing), or mark it complete. Reuses the shared API token config with the rest of the Teamwork plugin family. Never runs git, never logs time without confirmation, never silently overwrites an estimate, never moves the board or completes the task without asking. Since 1.3.0 tasks can be created from zsh and macOS bash 3.2 again (bash-4.4-only quoting had made every create fail), subtask mode reads the parent's project from `.tasklist.meta.projectId` so the board move can no longer pick another project's workflow, every failed read prints a warning instead of looking empty, and an explicit `false` in the config (e.g. is_billable_by_default) is no longer flipped back to `true`. The board move now lands in Done - Local on the new WAME board (shared keys migrated only where they still hold the old defaults). The drafted task carries the cross-cutting requirements shared with teamwork-task-test (reachability, security, performance, UI/UX) — claimed as delivered only when the diff proves it — and a technical-plan line recording the installed framework versions and the idioms the session actually used (plan only, never an acceptance criterion).

plugins.name: laravel-agents
plugins.description: Specialized Laravel subagents — laravel-backend, sql-database, api-architect, pest-tester, code-reviewer-laravel, security-auditor, performance-optimizer — plus four companion skills (wame-laravel-standards, wame-package-development, wame-security-checklist, wame-performance-playbook). The agents are thin personas of under 100 lines that defer to progressively-disclosed reference skills instead of inlining thousands of lines of examples: API response format (with BaseCollection pagination), database conventions (ULID, enums, sort, dateTimeTz, data via migrations not seeders), service layer, testing patterns, clean composer package/module creation per laravelpackage.com (stubs + composer.json path-repository wiring), OWASP Top 10 security checks, and a performance playbook. Nova-free by design — for Laravel Nova install laravel-nova-agents alongside. Migrated out of the old one-way lara-well/claude/config.sh copy mechanism so the agents version and update like any other plugin. Since 1.1.0 a shared cross-cutting quality reference applies the keys teamwork-task-test reviews at QA time while building: laravel-backend ships every new screen with its menu entry and inbound links, puts a policy and a FormRequest on every new entry point, eager-loads, paginates and indexes new lists, and writes new or changed code in the idioms of the installed Laravel / PHP / Pest versions (read from composer.lock, looked up via Laravel Boost search-docs or context7, each idiom tagged with its minimum version, no drive-by rewrites); pest-tester proves reachability and authorization with tests; code-reviewer-laravel reviews UI/UX, performance, security and reachability under the same keys and adds framework as advisory info recommendations — except an API newer than the installed version, which does not run and is a Critical finding.

plugins.name: laravel-nova-agents
plugins.description: The laravel-nova subagent for building Laravel Nova admin panels — BaseResource abstract class, custom Fields, Actions, Lenses, Filters, Metrics, CSV/Excel export, and Laravel Dusk browser tests — plus the companion wame-nova-patterns skill holding the Nova reference material and Dusk testing patterns. Install alongside laravel-agents: the pest-tester agent conditionally invokes wame-nova-patterns for Nova/Dusk browser testing only when this plugin is present, so non-Nova projects stay clean. Since 1.1.0 a Nova cross-cutting quality reference makes laravel-nova apply the keys teamwork-task-test checks while building: every new resource, lens, dashboard or tool is reachable from Nova::mainMenu() or a relation field on its parent, policies and tenant scope cover every query hook, search and index queries stay index-friendly, labels and help are translated and destructive actions confirmed, and Dusk tests reach new screens through the menu. New code follows the idioms of the installed Nova major (laravel/nova read from composer.lock, APIs looked up in current docs, a Nova 4 vs Nova 5 table checked against the vendor source), because Nova 5 code carried into a Nova 4 project fails on load; the BaseResource example now notes the Nova 4 query-hook signature.
